title: Scrapbook: Val Barbera's swing orchestra, 1936-37
summary: A 1937 photo of Val Barbera's band and an ad listing its members and novelties.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, this is 1950 you played. And here you are with Val Barbera.
Which gives you the right date, see?
1937, May the 23rd, Val Barbera and his famous swing orchestra. They were calling it swing then. Yeah. Well he had some tunes, but we still played some of the jazz tunes.
Most of the guys I played with, you'd always fake, we called them fake numbers, you know? They didn't use the word jazz too much maybe.

Yeah, I see Tom Brown and Luke Sciarro playing tenor there. Tom on bass. Yeah. He didn't lose trombone. Chicago trombone player. Cliff Curry playing alto. I guess he might be lead, I don't know. I don't think so. George Calder. Greg Terrio. Mike Costa playing alto too, it looks like. Well he was second trumpet player, Mike, at that time. Mike Costa was second, I got confused, yeah.
Well he plays, he ended up playing saxophone though as he got older.
Oh yeah, I see. And then George Calder is the alto player.

And there you are hidden away on the back, next to the piano player, Marce Saskat. And Red Norman. Red Noonan. Noonan, I can't read. He's playing guitar. Yeah. And Mrs. Barbera playing. I see the photo. Blackout.
Blackout. She was a singer, huh?

Yeah. That's 1936. She did sing. Oh, they have Tom Brown and his talking bass on the right arm. Yeah. George Calder, saxophone novelties. Stuart Bergen and his hot trumpet, Clarence Nunn guitar. Morris Esquiat piano wizard. The bar barrel was strictly commercial, wasn't it? Yeah. Ten or six piece orchestras as desired. Here's the band with Harry Shields and Gene Emott and John Wall.
